newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil outlines 15-year cellphone concession areas.
newsitem.headline: Brazil outlines 15-year cellphone concession areas.

text.p: Brazil has delineated the 10 areas nationwide where it will offer 15-year concessions to operate B Band cellular services and plans to publish bid specifications in the coming days, officials said.
The Communications Ministry said in a statement that winning bidders will be able to extend the 15-year concession contracts for equivalent periods.

In a sign of widespread investor interest in Brazil's B Band concessions, some 20 foreign-led groups have expressed an interest in taking part in auctions that will open up the country's promising cellular market to foreign capital.
The government hopes to begin the tender process and start granting concession contracts in mid-1997.

The statement said the government will offer one concession to operate in the metropolitan Sao Paulo area, another covering the rest of Sao Paulo state and a third over Rio de Janeiro and Espiritu Santo states.
A fourth concession area will cover Minas Gerais state, a fifth southern Parana and Santa Catarina states and a sixth Rio Grande do Sul state, it said.

Goais, Tocantins, Mato Grosso, Rondonia and Acre states and the federal district will be included in one concession area while the northern states of Amazonas, Roraima, Amapa, Para and Maranhao will comprise another, it added.

Area No. 9 will encompass Bahia and Sergipe states while the tenth will be made up of the poor northeastern states of Piaui, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco and Alagoas, the statement said.
The government plans "in the coming days" to publish the bid specifications, including base price, concession auction dates and other tender details, it said.
A ministry decree to be published Tuesday said the offering of cellular concessions are aimed at drawing new private investment in the sector and meeting high demand for cellular services in Brazil.
